Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is the section of our questionnaire focused on audit trails, retention, and exportability (Polestar_RFP_Section_C_audit_logs.xlsx). High-level asks in this section: retention tiers (30/90/365 days), ability to export bulk slices on demand, tamper-evidence for handed-off bundles, and chain-of-custody metadata for each export. We also need to understand delivery windows for large exports (up to 20TB) and whether you support direct S3 transfer into our bucket or prefer signed URLs. 

Target procurement timeline: answers returned by EOD Friday 2027-09-10. If you can provide an initial response and a short call to review technical constraints, that would be great. CCing procurement@polestarfinance.com for scheduling.

Appreciate the RFP section; we’ll treat this as high priority. Quick plan:
- Today: initial written responses to your spreadsheet (see attached high-level PDF)
- Tomorrow: technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Ben) to cover large-export mechanics and S3 onboarding

Short answers up front: Redwood supports configurable retention tiers (per-customer policies), on-demand bulk exports, and tamper-evident packaging (signed manifests + SHA256 checksums). From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-07T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Audit Log Export & Retention — Polestar Finance (internal)

Team —

Notes for the call / responses to the spreadsheet:
1) Retention windows: We support policy-based retention at the account and route level. Typical presets are 30, 90, 365 days; we can do custom windows and legal-hold overrides. Exports include full event metadata (timestamp, model_id, request_id, user_id hash, route, policy_version).

2) Export formats: NDJSON line-delimited events (preferred for streaming), optional CSV summaries for high-level reconciliation, and compressed tarballs (gz) for bulk. Example packaging: audit_dump_schema.ndjson.gz + accompanying s3_export_manifest.json which contains checksums, object list, and signed manifest metadata.

3) Delivery mechanics: For large transfers we prefer cross-account S3 Role (we assume write access to a pre-provisioned bucket). If customer cannot grant a role, we can deliver via multipart uploads to a Redwood-controlled bucket and provide presigned GET URLs for download. For 20TB jobs we split into segment batches (default 100GB parts) and provide an ordered manifest for replay.

4) Tamper evidence / chain of custody: Each bundle includes a signed manifest (Ed25519) with a Redwood-signed certificate chain. We also include per-object SHA256 and an overall Merkle root in the manifest metadata for quick verification. We keep a retention snapshot and audit log documenting when exports were initiated and completed (with operator id + job id).

5) SLAs & windows: On-demand exports are best-effort during normal operation; large bulk exports (>= 5TB) require scheduling into an export window. We can commit a 48-hour reserved window for contracted Dedicated customers; for hosted accounts we offer expedited batching with variable lead time.

I’ll prepare the s3_export_manifest_example.json and a short example of the signed manifest format for tomorrow’s call.

—Ben
Head of Production Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: s3_export_manifest_example.json (stub), audit_dump_schema.ndjson.gz (example)

Key summary (short):
- Retention: configurable 30/90/365 day presets + custom windows; legal-hold supported.
- Export formats: NDJSON (line-delimited) primary; CSV summary optional; tar.gz bundles for bulk.
- Delivery: preferred cross-account S3 role (fastest), fallback to presigned URLs. We support segmented multipart exports for multi-TB jobs.
- Tamper evidence: signed manifests (Ed25519), per-object SHA256, Merkle root.
- SLA: For multi-TB reserved windows we can commit a start-time & throughput target under a paid addendum.
